claims.text: Conventional heating requires temperatures above 2300 °C to fully densify ZrB2 powder.
High-temperature conventional sintering of ZrB2 produces coarse grain structures.
Lower-temperature conventional processing limits ZrB2 performance in oxidative or corrosive environments.
SPS can consolidate single-phase ZrB2 at approximately 1500 °C, significantly below 1700 °C.
SPS-processed ZrB2 can preserve or enhance mechanical integrity relative to conventionally sintered and prior lower-temperature ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 can improve oxidation resistance relative to conventionally sintered and prior lower-temperature ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 can improve liquid plating-metal corrosion durability relative to conventionally sintered and prior lower-temperature ZrB2.
Rapid SPS heating and short dwell times limit grain growth in ZrB2.
The proposed SPS process produces a fine-grained ZrB2 microstructure with minimized porosity and defect density.
SPS pulsed electric current and high heating rates accelerate diffusion and densification at lower temperatures.
The fine-grained, dense SPS microstructure preserves strong Zr–B and B–B interactions.
The SPS-derived microstructure promotes formation of a more uniform and adherent protective oxide scale during service.
A more uniform and adherent oxide scale improves the oxidation resistance of SPS-processed ZrB2.
Reduced porosity and defect density provide fewer pathways for liquid-metal penetration.
Reduced liquid-metal penetration enhances corrosion durability in a liquid plating-metal bath.
The proposed improvements are expected to persist in oxidative service at temperatures up to approximately 2000 °C.
The proposed improvements are expected to persist during extended exposure to a liquid plating-metal bath.
